title: Hermes Arcana field evidence
working_hypothesis: Lexicon + Arcana appears most useful when repository uncertainty is structural, and adds little once the working set is already narrow and directly searchable.

positive_or_boundary_cases.contribution: connected duplicated fallback policy and credential-pool state across Desktop and live-agent paths
narrowed writer class and exposed missing TypeScript callable/call graph coverage
eliminated ordinary static write paths and justified switch to runtime SQL tracing
mapped Gateway-to-CLI ownership coupling and migration seams
supported verification of micro-compaction persistence/call structure

low_benefit_or_control_cases.observation: direct source inspection sufficient while Lexicon/Arcana unavailable
compact working set; structured graph discovery not materially necessary
localized behavior; direct inspection and regression test sufficient
full structural machinery unnecessary until ownership analysis became the bottleneck

limitations: public outcomes do not isolate causal contribution
investigations mixed Arcana with ordinary developer tools

observations: effective refactor unit shifted from files to ownership domains
structural evidence influenced extraction order and hard-cut sequencing
distant cross-layer consumers remained a material source of refactor risk
graph structure did not replace behavioral, packaging, runtime, or review verification
negative structural evidence helped change diagnostic mode
structural blast-radius visibility appeared to reduce the uncertainty cost of hard-cut ownership moves
follow_up.updated_interpretation: During broad Hermes refactors, Arcana's main observed contribution is repository-scale architectural situational awareness: ownership, dependency direction, cross-layer consumers, and blast radius can affect refactor boundaries and sequencing before code is moved.
reciprocal_product_evidence: real Hermes use exposed missing TypeScript/TSX callable and call coverage
Hermes scale exposed incremental/shared-relationship and materialization problems
the packed graph remained about 47 MB; repository metadata and object lifetimes were the dominant storage/memory problem
stale generated Arcana state can become unusable when the query implementation advances format expectations
